answer: Each agent may claim only one slot in a rotating market, and claiming it requires a bond locked for a week. Agents earn reputation through tasks that randomly pair them with peers; a peer can challenge a result, but loses a small stake if the challenge fails. If a cluster of fake identities endorses one another, audits sample their shared work and slash bonds when endorsements prove collusive. The pearl, umber, and meadow markets use separate peer pools, so an attacker must fund many bonded identities and keep them active long enough to build trust, risking real capital for each one.
